signals.evidence: SearchAlertDrainerWorker marks saved-search alerts permanently delivered even when no real notification is sent, creating a silent-loss trap at the transport cutover. The drainer defaults to `LogEmailTransport`/`LogPushTransport` (backend/servers/reality-server/src/services/search_alert_drainer.rs:181-224), whose `send_email`/`send_push` ALWAYS return Ok(()). In `run_once` (lines 358-434) the email stub therefore always sets `any_ok = true`, so every alert row gets `mark_search_alert_notified(alert.id)` (sets notified_at) despite nothing actually leaving the process. This is documented as an intentional first cut, but the forward-looking hazard is NOT addressed: `list_undelivered_search_alerts` filters on notified_at, so when a real SMTP/FCM/APNs adapter is later injected via `with_transports`, every alert queued during the stub period is already notified_at != null and will be skipped forever — those users receive zero first real notification at cutover. Recommend either (a) gate `mark_search_alert_notified` on a transport that reports itself as real (add an `is_real()`/`enabled` seam to the transport traits so the log stubs do NOT advance notified_at), or (b) document a one-time reset of notified_at for the stub-era backlog as part of the real-transport rollout runbook.

evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/listings.rs:826-846 — `get_categories` (drives the reality-web homepage "Browse by category" tiles on the sk/cs/de/en portal) maps every `property_type` to a hardcoded SLOVAK label via `label_for_property_type` (listings.rs:823-846): apartment=>"Byty", house=>"Domy", land=>"Pozemky", commercial=>"Komerčné priestory", office=>"Kancelárie", garage=>"Garáže", parking=>"Parkovanie", storage=>"Sklady", with a `capitalize(other)` fallback for unknown types.

The doc comment at listings.rs:765-766 claims "Labels are returned in Slovak (primary market) — the frontend has its own i18n fallback if a label is missing." That justification is misleading: `label_for_property_type` NEVER returns an empty/missing label (the `other => capitalize(other)` arm guarantees a non-empty string for every input), so the promised frontend "missing-label fallback" can never trigger. A cs/de/en visitor therefore either sees Slovak category names, or the frontend must ignore the server `label` entirely and re-localize from `property_type` — in which case the `label` field is dead weight shipped in every response.

Impact: LOW (cosmetic i18n leak on a public marketing surface; no data/security impact). Confidence medium: the server behaviour is confirmed by static read; whether cs/de/en users actually SEE the Slovak text depends on whether reality-web renders `CategoryCount.label` or re-keys off `CategoryCount.property_type` (not runtime-confirmed here). Landable backend-only fix (no build-time codegen touched): either (a) drop the `label` field and let the client localize from the stable `property_type` enum (mirrors how the rest of the portal handles enum display), or (b) return a per-locale label keyed off an `Accept-Language`/`locale` query param. Option (a) is the smaller, safer change and removes the misleading comment.

get_categories (routes/listings.rs:776-820, GET /api/v1/listings/categories, public/anonymous endpoint) populates each CategoryCount.label via label_for_property_type (:822-837), which is a hardcoded Slovak-only match: apartment->"Byty", house->"Domy", land->"Pozemky", commercial->"Komerčné priestory", office->"Kancelárie", garage->"Garáže", parking->"Parkovanie", storage->"Sklady". The CategoryCount.label field doc-comment (:569-570) even states 'Localized display label (Slovak — primary market)', confirming this is a known single-locale shortcut. The handler takes only State (:776-778) — no Accept-Language header, no locale query param — so the Slovak labels are returned identically to every caller.

reality-web renders these labels directly (CategoryCount matches the client's CategoryCount type per :561) and ships six locale bundles (sk, cs, de, en, hu, pl). Because the label is pre-localized to Slovak server-side rather than returned as a translatable key, a cs/de/en/hu/pl portal user sees Slovak category names ('Byty', 'Domy', ...) with no client-side path to translate them. The `icon` field already returns the raw property_type key (:811) — i.e. the untranslated enum key IS available to the client — so the correct shape is to let the client translate the property_type key and drop (or make optional/locale-negotiated) the server-baked Slovak label.

Distinct from the sibling get_suggestions finding (different handler, different endpoint, different fix) and from all prior reality-server findings (no signal or backlog row references label_for_property_type / get_categories). Fix: either return only the property_type key and let reality-web's next-intl bundles localize it, or negotiate the label off an Accept-Language header instead of hardcoding Slovak. IG3: /api/v1/listings/categories with Accept-Language: en (or de) asserts labels are not the Slovak literals (or that the response exposes the raw property_type key for client-side translation).

Confidence medium: the Slovak-only match arm and the locale-unaware handler signature are confirmed by static read; severity low (+1) — a pure i18n label gap on a public helper endpoint (no auth, no correctness/region impact beyond display language), lower than the get_suggestions finding which additionally serves wrong-region city data.

The agency import-history handler (routes/agency_imports.rs, around :165-190) runs a hand-written query `SELECT ... FROM portal_import_jobs WHERE agency_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 100` (:170-176) and then reports `let total = rows.len() as i64;` (:183) as the response total. There is no offset/limit query param and no count query: the endpoint hard-caps the returned history at 100 rows and sets total = min(actual_rows, 100).

Consequence: once an agency accumulates more than 100 import jobs, the import-history view silently drops everything older than the 100 most-recent, and `total` misreports the real number of jobs as 100 — there is no pagination affordance and no signal to the client that the list was truncated. For a busy agency running recurring feed imports this hides the bulk of the audit trail. Lower severity than the imports.rs:131 finding because the truncation is a fixed cap (no client-side page-count miscomputation), but it is a distinct handler and a distinct silent-data-loss-on-read defect.

Fix: either add real pagination (limit+offset params + a COUNT(*) for total, mirroring list_import_jobs once that is corrected) or, at minimum, surface a `truncated`/`has_more` flag and derive total from a COUNT(*) rather than rows.len(). IG3: an integration test seeding >100 portal_import_jobs for one agency asserts the response exposes the true count (or a has_more flag) instead of a flat total==100.

Confidence medium: the LIMIT 100 literal and total=rows.len() are confirmed by static read; medium severity capped at +1 because the surface is membership-gated (check_agency_membership at :168) and the impact is truncated read visibility rather than a crash or cross-tenant leak.

list_import_jobs (routes/imports.rs:115-135, GET /api/v1/imports/jobs) is a PAGINATED endpoint — it reads query.limit.unwrap_or(20) and clamp_offset_i32(query.offset) (:124-126) and fetches a single page via reality_portal_repo.list_import_jobs(user_id, status, limit, offset). It then computes the pagination total as `let total = jobs.len() as i64;` (:131) and returns ImportJobsResponse { jobs, total } (:133). total therefore equals the size of the CURRENT PAGE (at most `limit`, default 20), NOT the true number of import jobs for the user.

Consequence: any client that computes page count as ceil(total / limit) sees total==20 on every full page (and total==remainder on the last), concludes there is exactly one page, and never requests offset=20,40,... — silently hiding every import job beyond the first page from the agency/realtor UI. On a user with, say, 55 import jobs the list appears to contain only 20. This is the same class of defect already confirmed in the sibling api-server compliance handler (code-review-api-handlers-user-audit-logs-total-page-len), here on the reality-server imports surface.

Fix: back total with a real count query (e.g. a reality_portal_repo.count_import_jobs(user_id, status) mirroring the filter), not the page length. IG3: an integration test seeding N>limit import jobs for one user asserts response.total == N while response.jobs.len() == limit. Distinct from the known 2026-08-31 reality-server pagination finding (which was about OFFSET integer overflow / clamping, since fixed via util::clamp_offset_i32 used right here at :126) — this is the response `total` field being wrong, an orthogonal bug.

Confidence medium: the paginated fetch (limit+offset) and the page-length-as-total computation are confirmed by static read of the full handler; medium (not high) because the surface is auth-gated (PortalPrincipal) and the harm is a corrupted pagination contract / under-exposed list rather than a crash, data loss, or cross-tenant leak.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/listings.rs:632 — `RichListingSummary.slug` (returned by the public /api/v1/listings/featured endpoint and consumed by the reality-web homepage to build listing URLs) is set to `slug: r.id.to_string()`, i.e. the raw listing UUID. The field is documented at listings.rs:523 ("URL slug — currently the listing UUID stringified (no slug column yet)") and listings.rs:629-631 ("No slug column on listings yet — the frontend treats the path").

For a PUBLIC real-estate portal where organic search traffic is a primary acquisition channel, UUID-based canonical URLs (/listings/8f3c...-uuid) are an SEO and shareability liability: no keyword signal in the path, opaque/untrustworthy-looking links in social shares and SERPs, and no human-readable fallback. signals.evidence: A realtor-facing DB write Result is silently discarded with no logging, so read-state desync is unobservable. In the realtor inquiry-detail path (backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/inquiries.rs:700-704) the code does `let _ = state.reality_portal_repo.mark_inquiry_read_for_realtor(id, principal.user_id).await;` — the Result of a DB UPDATE that marks the inquiry read is dropped entirely (no `?`, no `map_err`, no `tracing::warn`). Ownership is already verified above so this is not an authz bug, but unlike the truly fire-and-forget analytics call at listings.rs:370 (`track_view`), inquiry read-state is user-visible: if the UPDATE fails (transient DB error, deadlock, connection drop), the inquiry keeps showing as unread on every subsequent load with zero operator visibility into why. Contrast with the deliberate, commented discard in saved_search_alerts.rs:223. Recommend at minimum logging the failure (`if let Err(e) = ... { tracing::warn!(inquiry_id = %id, error = %e, "failed to mark inquiry read"); }`) so the desync is diagnosable.

Saved-search alert matching silently drops matches beyond `config.match_limit` (default 100) in a single cadence window. The worker calls `find_new_match_listing_ids(&query, Some(since), match_limit)` which runs `SELECT l.id ... WHERE l.published_at > $since ORDER BY l.published_at DESC LIMIT $limit` (backend/crates/db/src/repositories/reality_portal/searches.rs:102-121) — returning only the NEWEST `match_limit` matches. It then commits `enqueue_and_advance_saved_search`, whose `mark_saved_search_matched` unconditionally sets `last_matched_at = now()` (searches.rs:185-192). Because the watermark jumps to now() regardless of how many rows the capped query returned, any matching listing ranked 101+ in that window (i.e. published_at between `since` and the 100th-newest match) has published_at <= now() and is excluded from every subsequent run's `published_at > since` filter. Net effect: on a broad saved search over a daily/weekly cadence on an active portal (>100 new matching listings per window is realistic for e.g. 'apartments for rent in Bratislava'), the user is never notified about the older portion of the batch, and `match_count` also undercounts (incremented by the capped listing_ids.len()). Fix options: page the query and advance the watermark only to the oldest UNPROCESSED match's published_at when the cap is hit, or advance last_matched_at to the min(published_at) of the returned rows rather than now() when `rows.len() == match_limit`, so the next run resumes from the truncation boundary instead of skipping past it.

Mobile SSO entry point conflates a transient PM-side introspection outage with a genuinely invalid token, returning 401. `create_mobile_sso_token` (backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:450-499) calls `introspect_pm_token(...)` and maps ANY Err to `(StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, 'invalid_token')` (sso.rs:456-462). But `introspect_pm_token_inner` (sso.rs:796-857) was DELIBERATELY hardened to return an Err WITHOUT caching on any non-2xx introspection response — a PM 5xx outage, 502/504 gateway error, or transport error — precisely because such a response is 'not a genuine active=false verdict' (per the Epic 104.2 negative-cache-poisoning guard comment). The handler discards that carefully-preserved distinction: during a transient PM introspection outage a mobile client presenting a perfectly valid token receives 401 invalid_token, which signals 'your credentials are bad' and can cause the client to discard/clear otherwise-valid credentials and force a spurious re-login. The transport-layer effort to distinguish outage-from-inactive is negated at the handler boundary. Recommend surfacing PM outage/5xx/transport errors as 502 Bad Gateway or 503 Service Unavailable (retryable) rather than 401, so clients back off and retry instead of treating the token as invalid. The same collapse-to-401 also applies to the `get_user_info` failure branch (sso.rs:472-479) and `refresh_session` (sso.rs:613-626).

evidence: get_suggestions (routes/listings.rs:457-480, GET /api/v1/listings/suggestions, public/anonymous search-suggestions endpoint consumed by reality-web) returns a `popular_searches` list that is a hardcoded Slovak-only literal vec (:474-478): `"2-izbový byt Bratislava"`, `"Dom Košice"`, `"Pozemok Žilina"`. These are user-facing suggestion strings rendered verbatim by the client, and they are returned identically regardless of the caller's locale. reality-web ships SIX locale bundles (frontend/apps/reality-web/messages/: sk, cs, de, en, hu, pl), so a de/en/cs/hu/pl portal visitor is shown Slovak search suggestions with no way to localize them — the strings are baked server-side, not returned as translatable keys.

The same handler hardcodes the nearby-city fallback to a Slovak city: `let city = params.get("city")...unwrap_or("Bratislava")` (:461-464), then feeds it to `get_nearby_cities(city, 10)` (:466-468). reality-server is explicitly multi-region (backend/CLAUDE.md + REGION env supports sk/cz/eu; reality-portal.cz and reality-portal.eu are first-class default CORS origins), so on a Czech (.cz) or EU (.eu) deployment a suggestion request that omits `city` seeds nearby-city suggestions from Bratislava (SK) rather than a region-appropriate default — wrong-country content, not merely untranslated. This is a region-awareness correctness defect on top of the i18n gap.

Distinct from every prior reality-server finding: the recent i18n finding (alert-drainer-i18n-english-only, 2026-08-30) is in services/search_alert_drainer.rs + email.rs, and the prior listings.rs findings (viewcount-hardcoded-zero, orphan-listinghandler-stub-detail, pagination-offset-overflow — all done) touch different handlers. No prior signal or backlog row references get_suggestions / popular_searches. Fix: return `popular_searches` as translatable keys (or derive them from actual popular queries per region) instead of Slovak literals, and make the default city region-derived (from REGION / host) rather than the constant "Bratislava". IG3: a request to /api/v1/listings/suggestions on a non-SK region (or with an Accept-Language other than sk) asserts the suggestions/default-city are not the Slovak Bratislava literals.

Confidence medium: the hardcoded Slovak literals and the Bratislava default are confirmed by static read of the full handler; severity medium (+2) rather than low because the Bratislava default produces wrong-region content on the cz/eu deployments (a correctness issue), not only an untranslated string — but not high because the endpoint is a non-critical public suggestions helper (no auth, no data loss, no crash).

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/listings.rs:472-480 — the public `get_suggestions` handler (GET /api/v1/listings/suggestions, autocomplete/search-suggestions surface) returns `popular_searches` as a HARDCODED three-element vec: ["2-izbový byt Bratislava", "Dom Košice", "Pozemok Žilina"]. The `cities` half of the response is real (derived from `portal_repo.get_nearby_cities`), but `popular_searches` is a static stub shipped on a production public endpoint — it is not derived from any search-frequency/analytics data, so it is not actually 'popular', and it never changes regardless of market activity.

Two problems compound: (1) completeness — the field's name promises data-driven popular searches but delivers a fixed literal, so the feature is effectively unimplemented behind a real-looking API contract; (2) i18n — the three strings are Slovak-only literals on a sk/cs/de/en portal, so a cs/de/en visitor's suggestion box shows Slovak example queries.

Impact: LOW (a public marketing/UX surface; no data or security impact). Confidence medium (static read is definitive on the stub; user-visible effect depends on whether reality-web renders `popular_searches`). Landable backend-only fix: either wire `popular_searches` to a real source (e.g. a top-N aggregation over recent saved-search / search-event rows, or the existing search-analytics tables), or, if that data is not yet available, drop the field from the response contract rather than shipping a hardcoded Slovak stub. If kept as a placeholder, at minimum localize per request locale.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-10 reality-web listing-detail AdditionalInfo section formats prices with a locally-redefined formatPrice hardcoded to en-US, wrong for every sk/cs/de/pl/hu visitor)
evidence: AdditionalInfo.tsx:8-16 -- the section defines its OWN module-local `formatPrice(price, currency)` that calls `new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', ...)` on BOTH branches (the no-currency fallback at :11 and the currency branch at :12-15). The locale is hardcoded to 'en-US' regardless of the visitor's route locale, so on the public, SEO-indexed listing-detail page a Slovak/Czech/German buyer sees US-formatted money (comma thousands + '.' decimals + '$'-style symbol placement) instead of `1 234 €` / `1.234 €`. This is a customer-facing correctness defect on the money field of the primary listing page.

This directly re-introduces the anti-pattern the codebase's shared helper was built to kill: lib/format.ts header (:1-17) states it 'Replaces scattered Number#toLocaleString(...) / Intl.NumberFormat(\'en-US\', {...}) call sites that all hardcoded a single locale and produced visibly wrong output for the other five', and exposes `formatPrice(value, locale, options)` (lib/format.ts:48-59) that threads bcp47(locale) + defaults to EUR. AdditionalInfo bypasses it with an inline en-US copy.

The locale is trivially available in this component -- it is a `[locale]` route section and already calls `useTranslations('listing')` at :20, so `useLocale()` is in scope. The fix is frontend-only: delete the local formatPrice and import `formatPrice` from '@/lib/format', calling `formatPrice(price, locale, { currency })`.

Reproduce (static): grep -n "'en-US'" components/listings/sections/AdditionalInfo.tsx -> :11 and :12; grep -n 'import.*format' AdditionalInfo.tsx -> no import from lib/format. Contrast ListingCard.tsx:106 which correctly does `formatPrice(listing.price, locale, { currency: listing.currency })`.

Non-duplicate: verified against all 92 prior *reality-web*.json ids -- no prior id references AdditionalInfo or a hardcoded 'en-US' formatter. Distinct from code-review-reality-web-categorycards-tolocalestring-no-locale (that was a bare `toLocaleString()` on a homepage COUNT; this is an explicit `Intl.NumberFormat('en-US')` on a PRICE in the listing-detail section registry) and from the missing-string i18n findings. Confidence medium: the en-US hardcode is code-verified statically; exact rendered glyphs depend on the runtime Intl data, not run-confirmed.

AgencyBranding.tsx handleSave (L79-95) does `await updateBranding.mutateAsync({ agencyId, data: { logo, coverImage, primaryColor, ... } })` with NO try/catch, then resets hasChanges/logoFile/coverFile.

updateBranding is consumed only for `.isPending` (button label at L126/128); `updateBranding.error` is NEVER rendered. On a failed branding save the follow-up state resets never run (mutateAsync rejects), the user gets zero feedback, and it is an unhandled promise rejection.

The backing hook useUpdateBranding (agency/hooks.ts:258) posts multipart FormData (logo/coverImage uploads) and `throw new ApiError(response.status)` on !response.ok (L276-278), with onSuccess-only (no onError) at L282. Image uploads are exactly the path that fails with 413 (payload too large) / 415 / 500, so a silent failure here is likely in practice.

This file already distinguishes load errors carefully (AgencyLoadError on agencyError, Issue #2343) but the write path has no equivalent handling. Fix: wrap mutateAsync in try/catch, keep hasChanges true on failure, and render an inline error (updateBranding.error / a caught message) near the save button, consistent with the sibling error-state handling in the same component.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-10 reality-web AgencyDashboard defines a local locale-less formatNumber with hardcoded English K/M magnitude suffixes, shadowing the shared locale-aware helper)
evidence: AgencyDashboard.tsx:889-893 defines a module-local `function formatNumber(num: number): string` that returns `${(num/1000000).toFixed(1)}M` / `${(num/1000).toFixed(1)}K` / `num.toString()`. It (a) hardcodes English magnitude suffixes 'K'/'M' -- a German/Slovak agency owner sees English abbreviations; (b) uses toFixed which forces a '.' decimal separator regardless of locale (de/sk use ','); (c) for values < 1000 emits bare `num.toString()` with no locale grouping. It is used for the stat cards at :402 `value: formatNumber(stats.totalViews)` (called with ONE arg, so it resolves to this local fn, NOT the shared one).

This shadows and contradicts lib/format.ts#formatNumber(value, locale, options) (:38-45), the app's designated locale-aware helper whose header (:1-17) exists precisely to replace 'scattered ... call sites that all hardcoded a single locale'. The shared fn requires a locale arg; the local one takes none, which is why the single-arg call at :402 silently binds to the wrong function.

The component already imports next-intl useTranslations (:17) and is a `[locale]` route, so `useLocale()` is available to thread. frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/auth/login/page.tsx:33,72-73 — the login form reads its post-login destination from a user-controlled query param (`const redirectTo = searchParams.get('redirect') ?? The guard rejects absolute URLs (`http://…`) and protocol-relative `//evil.com`, but it does NOT reject the backslash-escape form `/\evil.com`. Browsers normalise `\` to `/` during URL resolution, so `router.replace('/\evil.com')` resolves to `//evil.com` → a protocol-relative navigation to an attacker origin. An attacker who gets a victim to open `https://<tenant>/sk/auth/login?redirect=/%5Cevil.example.com` and log in is silently bounced to evil.example.com immediately after authenticating — a classic post-auth open-redirect / phishing primitive.

The SIBLING callback page proves this is a real, known vector and that the login page simply missed it: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/auth/callback/page.tsx:116-125 guards the same class of redirect param with THREE conditions — `rawRedirect.startsWith('/') && !rawRedirect.startsWith('//') && !rawRedirect.startsWith('/\\')` — and its test file callback/page.test.tsx:122-135 has dedicated cases 'rejects a protocol-relative redirect_uri' AND 'rejects a backslash-escaped redirect_uri (`/%5Cevil.example.com`)'. The login page's guard is the same idea with the third (`/\`) clause dropped, and no test exercises the login redirect at all.

Impact: open redirect on the primary email/password login flow across every tenant host. Severity medium (phishing enabler / reputational — requires the victim to follow a crafted link and complete login; no direct data compromise). Confidence high: the full path is traced from the user-controlled `searchParams.get('redirect')` to `router.replace(safe)`, the missing clause is confirmed by direct diff against the tested sibling guard, and reachability is trivial (any anonymous visit to the login URL). Fix: extract the callback's 3-way check into one shared `isSafeInternalRedirect(path)` helper (reject non-`/` prefixes, `//`, and `/\`, and ideally decode-then-recheck) and use it in BOTH login/page.tsx:72 and callback/page.tsx:122-124; add the `/\evil.com` rejection test to the login page mirroring callback/page.test.tsx:129.
